metabolism.title: Metabolism
metabolism.inactive: Metabolism is inactive in this mode
metabolism.help.protein: Building material for muscle and tissue. A long shortage reduces recovery potential.
metabolism.help.fat: Energy and essential fatty acids needed for a balanced diet.
metabolism.help.carb: Fast fuel that replenishes energy reserves.
metabolism.help.fiber: Plant fiber supports digestion; a shortage lowers diet quality.
metabolism.help.vitamin_b12: Supports nerves and blood cell formation.
metabolism.help.iron: Needed for oxygen transport. Currently contributes to diet quality.
metabolism.help.calcium: Important for bones and muscles. Currently contributes to diet quality.
metabolism.help.anatomical_hp: Current and maximum HP summed from Trauma body regions. Metabolism does not modify HP.
metabolism.help.vanilla_hp: Trauma data unavailable. Shows Minecraft health without conversion to anatomical HP.
metabolism.help.quality: Ten nutrient adequacy values. A severe shortage reduces the score even when other nutrients are abundant.
metabolism.help.energy: Combined fast and fat energy reserves, not a separate stamina bar.
metabolism.help.toxins: Hazardous food adds toxins. They clear over time and reduce absorption and recovery potential.
metabolism.help.glycogen: Game model of fast energy reserves spent on activity and metabolism.
metabolism.help.fat_reserve: Long-term energy reserve used when fast fuel runs out.
metabolism.help.stomach: Energy waiting to be digested relative to the game's stomach capacity.
metabolism.help.absorption: Fraction of nutrients the body can use; toxins reduce it.
metabolism.help.recovery: Multiplier for future Trauma integration, not actual healing or HP/min.
metabolism.help.resistance: Multiplier for future medical integration. Does not directly alter disease.
metabolism.help.burn: Calories per in-game hour at current movement, including basal metabolism.
metabolism.help.fatigue: WorldLogic Core fatigue readout. Metabolism does not store a second stamina bar.
metabolism.help.vitamins: Average adequacy of vitamins A, C and B12; each is listed separately.
metabolism.help.minerals: Average adequacy of iron, calcium and magnesium; each is listed separately.
metabolism.help.deficits: Number of nutrients below 60% of their target. Surplus of another nutrient cannot replace them.
metabolism.help.critical: Number of nutrients below 25% of target, limiting recovery.
metabolism.help.fast_time: Estimated game hours at current expenditure, excluding food and fat fuel.
metabolism.help.total_time: Estimated game hours of stored energy at current expenditure, not a starvation death prediction.
metabolism.help.digestion_time: Estimated game hours until the stomach empties at its current rate. Toxins and low fiber slow digestion.
metabolism.trend_help: Arrow compares the level with a smoothed one-game-day baseline; = means stable or insufficient data.
metabolism.food.unknown: Unknown food profile; energy is estimated
metabolism.food.macros: P %s g | F %s g | C %s g | Fiber %s g
metabolism.help.water: Water level from Hydration. ? means unavailable.
metabolism.help.salts: Hydration index: 50 is balanced; deviations reduce absorption.
metabolism.help.body_temp: Body temperature from Thermal, not air temperature.
metabolism.help.thermal_cost: Energy expenditure multiplier for body temperature deviation.
metabolism.help.water_factor: Digestion multiplier based on water and salts. Neutral without Hydration.
metabolism.help.tissue_factor: Repair potential from protein, vitamin C and energy; applied by integrated Trauma.
metabolism.help.bone_factor: Bone recovery potential based on calcium and nutrition.
metabolism.help.blood_factor: Blood recovery potential from iron and B12.
metabolism.help.today_intake: Accepted meal calories this active game day.
metabolism.help.today_burn: Energy spent during the current active game day.
metabolism.help.history_day_1: Intake / expenditure in kcal; bar and color represent mean diet quality. One day is 1200 active seconds.
metabolism.help.history_day_2: Intake / expenditure in kcal; bar and color represent mean diet quality. One day is 1200 active seconds.
metabolism.help.history_day_3: Intake / expenditure in kcal; bar and color represent mean diet quality. One day is 1200 active seconds.
metabolism.help.history_day_4: Intake / expenditure in kcal; bar and color represent mean diet quality. One day is 1200 active seconds.
metabolism.help.history_day_5: Intake / expenditure in kcal; bar and color represent mean diet quality. One day is 1200 active seconds.
metabolism.help.history_day_6: Intake / expenditure in kcal; bar and color represent mean diet quality. One day is 1200 active seconds.
metabolism.help.history_day_7: Intake / expenditure in kcal; bar and color represent mean diet quality. One day is 1200 active seconds.
metabolism.help.hp_rate: Measured passive anatomical HP repair over up to 60 active seconds, excluding instant treatments. ? means unavailable or insufficient samples.
